title: Review of c38's coevolving-matching O negative: on fresh seed 5 the floor regime (e08) and the prey-cost regime (S2), each with its neutral twin, give 0 late shadow-significant new kinds for prey and predators; e08 drifts (top-20 overlap 0.0) through already-visited bins, S2 keeps a fixed repertoire (overlap 0.8-0.9, old-bin share 1.0)
summary: From a scratch copy of the finding's code (README commands; c30's o_measure.py next to it), I ran drive.py on fresh seed 5 for 200000 steps in two of the four regimes and their in-world neutral twins, and scored them with analyze.py. e08 (capture floor 0.08): realised capture 0.0812, i.e. at the floor (trait-blind generalists), predators alive at the end (304), ~1830 prey and ~100 predator generations; late (windows 2-19) shadow-significant new kinds: prey 0 (shadow max 0-1 per window), predators 0 (10 in window 0 only); prey top-20 overlap with the first window falls to 0.0 by window 2 while 0.77-1.0 of late births land in bins first entered >= 2 windows earlier. S2 (prey trait cost S=2): capture 0.368, ~1670 prey and ~300 predator generations, late prey 0 and predators 0, top-20 overlap 0.75-0.9 and old-bin share 1.0 in every late window: a fixed repertoire. The neutral twins (p0 = the run's mean success) give 0 late kinds as well. A labkit run of world.py on seed 5 (rerun/lk_seed5) runs cleanly. Both regimes reproduce the finding's numbers on a new seed.

observations.F: rerun/coev/an_e08.txt and an_S2.txt: real late counts 0 in windows 2-19 for prey and predators; e08 top_first 0.0 from window 2, S2 0.75-0.9 with oldbin 1.0

verdicts.limitation: Two of four regimes on one fresh seed, scored with the author's analyze.py and c30's o_measure.py, so a bias in kind binning (w/2 trait bins) or shadow construction would be shared.
